summary: The selected browser board can move one existing root item through its row menu. store::move_group_item checks current write access via the enclosing selected-board transaction, locks the item and active groups, and advances only the item revision and group stamp when the group changes. The v5 migration preserves creation provenance and gives grouped and flat reads the same position, creation-time and UUID ordering.
evidence: browser_moves_item_by_group_id passed. The fixed-board dialog offered Work, Reserve, Work with values g-90, g-10, g-20. Choosing the last Work and cancelling sent no PUT. Confirming once with the destination locked showed Saving and the old counts. Release produced one PUT 200 and one grouped GET. Board 201 then showed g-90=[73], empty Reserve and g-20=[61,59], matching the reference fixture. Reconnect confirmed that only 61's group, revision and group stamp changed; position 2, timestamp, title and creator were preserved. Reload resolved the same session and fetched that board once at the same history entry without replay.

browser_demoted_viewer_cannot_move_item passed. Demotion after selection yielded one PUT 403 and a GET 200. Both Work sections retained their rows and counts. On reload the Viewer could open the row menu but Move to was disabled. Independent checks covered all item and group records, the direct and sibling boards, grants, role and original session.

browser_reviews_failed_group_move passed. A deferred constraint failed at commit (500); independent reads before fault removal found the original state and stamp. Review read g-90 and g-20 without writing; Dismiss sent no request. After fault removal, explicit Apply sent one new PUT and the accepted order survived reload. A peer move before dialog open required review without a PUT; another peer change after review produced 409 on Apply without overwriting it.

preview_move_requires_current_group_access passed for absent and revoked sessions, Viewer and withdrawn membership, inactive source, missing and foreign items, and invalid or newly archived destinations. Rejections returned no item details and fresh connections found unchanged rows. Native, scoped and non-preview paths did not expose the operation.

preview_move_checks_group_revision_and_order passed: a move across a rename preserved Coral; a same-group no-op kept both revisions; future, zero and stale group revisions including a round trip could not write. Grouped and flat reads agreed for distinct-time and same-time ties. Append into the tied group kept both existing rows. Creation replay used the original group and returned the current row; claiming the new group as its creation scope failed. Migrating populated v4 twice preserved IDs, names, order, revisions and provenance without inventing old creation dates.

Final serial headless browser_preview run: 17 passed, including all 14 inherited journeys. Serial loopback_board_access: 17 passed. Locked workspace tests: 32 passed. Cargo used target-browser-packets. Workspace formatting and git diff --check passed. The worker shell denied node --test scripts/run.test.mjs before execution, so Node runner regressions remain unverified here.
